description: I am a Systems Engineering student passionate about technology, AI, programming, and space exploration. I enjoy developing innovative solutions and applying software to real-world challenges. I bring skills in software development and data analysis, and I am looking to collaborate with creative, motivated people with backgrounds in science, engineering, electronics, and design.
summary:
BLUE FLAME is a web dashboard that organizes NASA's 24 PSI combustion studies (19 flight experiments and 5 ground-based studies) into comparable data. Users configure environments such as space stations or lunar bases by adjusting oxygen, pressure, materials, gravity, and ventilation. The dashboard dynamically displays flame behavior and safety recommendations.

Its Coverage and Scope sections compare fire favorability with the ISS, identify relevant experiments, and reveal unexplored conditions through an interactive map.

We used NASA's public metadata, Python, Docker, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Claude API to extract and verify experimental data, preserving citations to original sources. Over 50 automated tests validate the evaluation rules.

BLUE FLAME transforms hours of technical research into seconds, helping engineers assess fire safety during habitat design, researchers identify knowledge gaps, and students understand combustion in microgravity. Its calculations use transparent, reproducible rules rather than real-time AI.
details:
BLUE FLAME is a web-based dashboard that transforms microgravity combustion experiments from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database into clear, actionable insights for fire safety in space. We brought together all 24 combustion studies in PSI (19 flight experiments and 5 ground-based studies) and described them using the same fields and units: fuel, oxygen, pressure, airflow, safety functions, and others. Users define a scenario by selecting an environment, such as the International Space Station, a lunar base, or a pressurized rover, and adjusting oxygen, pressure, material, gravity, and ventilation. The dashboard is organized into four tabs: Experiment allows users to configure a scenario and see an illustrated flame and recommendations for fire prevention, detection, and suppression in real time; Coverage features a thermometer showing how favorable the scenario is for a fire compared to the ISS, along with the five factors explaining the result and research studies ranked by relevance; Scope identifies conditions and combinations that have never been investigated in any experiment; and the Conditions Map positions the scenario against all existing research on an oxygen-versus-pressure chart. All calculations use explainable rules based on published experimental results and supported by cited sources, without relying on real-time artificial intelligence.

As a result, what previously required hours of reading technical documents can now be done in seconds. The dashboard makes it possible to compare studies that were previously difficult to compare, connects experiments with real exploration environments, and identifies knowledge gaps. It is also transparent: each study shows how its data were extracted, whether the team has verified it, any warnings, and a link to its original PSI source. Each fire-favorability factor also cites the publication supporting it. In addition, the "What Would You Change?" feature shows which adjustment, such as lowering oxygen levels or using fire-resistant materials, produces the greatest reduction in fire favorability, giving the tool a preventive rather than merely informational approach.

This approach is particularly important for the future of space exploration. Upcoming lunar bases and pressurized rovers will use atmospheres with higher oxygen concentrations and lower pressure than the ISS, making materials more flammable. BLUE FLAME helps engineers and habitat designers assess these scenarios from the earliest design stages, enables researchers to identify missing experiments, such as the lack of partial-gravity combustion data in PSI, and helps teachers and students visually understand how fire behaves in space. It also contributes to fire safety on Earth, where NASA research has already improved fire extinguishers, smoke detection systems, and firefighting equipment.

To build the project, we processed the data using Python in a Docker-based workflow that downloads PSI's public metadata, extracts the characterization of each study, and, when AI is used for extraction, verifies that every data point is supported by the original text. The dashboard was developed using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript organized into modules, with Vite as the development tool and more than 50 automated tests to validate the rules. We used Git for version control and Visual Studio Code as our development environment. We also leveraged artificial intelligence tools: Claude, by Anthropic, for code design and development, and ChatGPT to generate the logo image. All design decisions, rules, and results were reviewed by the team.

What makes this project creative is that, instead of presenting a list of documents, it starts with the user's question: "I have this scenario. What do we know, and what don't we know?" The illustrated flame is not merely decorative; it changes according to observations from the experiments: it becomes spherical and blue in microgravity, elongated under Earth's gravity, larger and brighter with more oxygen, and goes out when there is insufficient oxygen to sustain combustion. Rather than providing an absolute risk score that we could not scientifically justify, we compare each scenario with the ISS atmosphere, an environment NASA already understands. We also turn information gaps into valuable results by showing exactly where further research is needed.

Throughout development, we were guided by three principles. Trust: Fire favorability is an indicative metric, not a substitute for NASA experiments. Every rule cites its source, and studies with incomplete data are flagged rather than hidden. Reproducibility: We use explainable rules instead of real-time AI, allowing anyone to obtain the same results, verify them, and use the tool free of charge. Accessibility: The dashboard supports keyboard navigation, dark mode, and reduced motion, is available in four languages, and works offline as a single file.
